findings.description: Keyless CLI dispatch now hard-depends on the shared openbao_credentials package. api_key_resolver.py imports it at module top, and review_dispatcher.py additionally runs `from openbao_credentials import BaoCredentialError` unconditionally inside dispatch_and_wait (line 2979), so the import executes even when every reviewer is a CLI vendor and BAO_ADDR is unset. The previous resolver imported hvac lazily inside the Bao branch and degraded gracefully. Every orchestrator skill (autopilot SKILL.md:175, iterate-on-implementation SKILL.md:482/507, parallel-review-plan SKILL.md:250, parallel-infrastructure SKILL.md:103) documents launching the dispatcher with plain `python3`, and the runtime copies under .agents/skills serve non-Claude harnesses with no skills/.venv. In this very worktree the skills venv has neither path dependency installed, so `python3 review_dispatcher.py` in pure CLI mode raises ImportError at dispatch time (the importlib fallback at lines 2940-2951 re-executes the module and propagates the same ImportError). This regresses CFG-02 (non-OpenBao profile remains compatible) and CFG-25 (CLI processes retain their existing contract). Fix: import openbao_credentials lazily inside the configured-Bao branch of resolve() and inside _resolve_dispatch_key's except clause (or catch a locally defined base), so absence of the package only matters when BAO_ADDR is set.
findings.resolution: Move the openbao_credentials imports into the BAO_ADDR-configured code path in ApiKeyResolver.resolve and into _resolve_dispatch_key; add a test that dispatch_and_wait with only CLI adapters succeeds when `openbao_credentials` is absent from sys.modules (patch.dict sys.modules with None).

findings.description: The SDK tier uses the pip package name (`sdk.package`) as the credential vendor id that is authorized against `vendor_credentials` and read at `vendors/<vendor>`. The registry's authorization vocabulary is the `credential_vendors` catalog (anthropic, openai, openrouter, xai). These coincide today only because the two dispatchable SDK agents use packages `anthropic` and `openai`. SdkVendorAdapter already supports `google-generativeai`, and a future xAI SDK agent would declare `vendor_credentials: [xai]` while its package would be `openai` or `xai-sdk`: the lookup would either always be denied, or an xAI request would be authorized under the `openai` scope and read the OpenAI vendor key. D1 states the catalog, not package or CLI fields, defines the vendor vocabulary. Not a blocker for the current registry, but the mapping should be explicit.
findings.resolution: Carry an explicit credential vendor id in the dispatch config (e.g. `sdk.credential_vendor`, or derive from the single-element vendor_credentials when unambiguous) rather than reusing the package name; add a test for a package/vendor mismatch being rejected at config load.

findings.existing_code:
# A keyless local endpoint has no credential to request.
if (openai_adapter.endpoint_kind == "local" and principal_id is None
    and not self.openai_key_envs.get(reviewer.agent_id)):
    api_key, lookup_error = None, None
else:
    api_key, lookup_error = _resolve_dispatch_key(principal_id, vendor_id)
findings.description: In configured-Bao mode an endpoint agent without a registry `api_key` (null principal) but with an `api_key_env`, or any openrouter agent without a registry key, is sent to `resolve(None, vendor)`, which raises CONFIGURATION_INVALID with category `principal`. Failing closed is correct per D2, but the surfaced error `OpenBao credential lookup failed: CONFIGURATION_INVALID` points the operator at Bao configuration when the actual cause is that the agent has no registry principal. There is no test for the openrouter-without-principal case.
findings.resolution: Short-circuit before the resolver when principal_id is None in configured mode and return a distinct AUTH error such as `agent has no registry principal; cannot request vendor credential`, and add a test for an openrouter agent with principal_id None under BAO_ADDR.

findings.description: The resolver re-derives the Bao role name (`agent-<name>`) from the SPIFFE ID with a private regex and f-string (line 47) instead of using the shared topology's encoding. D1 says name encoding is centralized in the openbao_credentials package. The duplicated rule matches today (same slug pattern as topology._SLUG and adapter._PRINCIPAL) but will drift silently if the role-name encoding ever changes. Acceptable for pca-02 given the resolver only has the principal id, not the registry.
findings.resolution: Optionally expose a `role_name_for_principal(principal_id)` helper from openbao_credentials.topology and call it here.

findings.description: The main skill-workflow spec still requires `ApiKeyResolver` to attempt OpenBao first using the agent's `openbao_role_id` and to fall back to the environment variable. This change ships deltas only for agent-coordinator, agent-identity, and configuration, so after archive the canonical spec will contradict the implemented `resolve(principal_id, vendor_id)` contract. Outside wp-dispatch's write scope; belongs to wp-integration or an update-specs pass.
findings.resolution: Add a skill-workflow delta (or update-specs follow-up) replacing the openbao_role_id resolution requirement with the principal-scoped contract.

findings.description: In non-Bao mode the resolver never consults `scopes`, so a vendor outside an agent's `vendor_credentials` still resolves from its configured env var. This is consistent with CFG-02 (development path unchanged) and no Bao read occurs, but the class docstring claims authorization happens before any read. Documenting that scope enforcement is configured-mode only would avoid a false sense of enforcement in dev.
findings.resolution: Clarify the docstring, or apply the scope check in both modes if the team wants dev parity.

findings.description: `credential_envs` is keyed by `(principal_id, vendor_id)`; two keyless SDK agents with the same package but different `api_key_env` collapse to one entry (last wins). Only affects the non-Bao development path and the current registry has no such pair, but keying by agent_id (as `credential_requests` already is) would remove the ambiguity.
findings.resolution: Key the env map by agent_id and look the tuple up per reviewer, or document the constraint.

findings.description: The worker's claim of 180 passing tests could not be independently reproduced: the sandbox denied the pytest invocation, and this worktree's skills/.venv has neither `openbao_credentials` nor `system_one_decisions` installed under site-packages although both are declared as path dependencies in skills/pyproject.toml and uv.lock. The package verification command as written would fail with ImportError in this worktree until `uv sync` is run in skills/. The orchestrator should re-run the verification step after syncing before accepting the evidence key `dispatch_tests_passed`.
findings.resolution: Run `cd skills && uv sync` then the verification command from work-packages.yaml, and record the actual count.
